newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat jumps on pool rise, crop cut and drought.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat jumps on pool rise, crop cut and drought.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) wheat futures rose strongly on Tuesday in reaction to the Australian Wheat Board's (AWB) pool price increase and crop downgrade on Monday night.
January 1998 traded A$4.00 a tonne higher at A$199.50 while March 1998 sold at A$202.00, up A$4.50. Settlement prices of untraded contracts rose by SA$4.00 to A$9.00.

This followed the AWB's announcement of a A$10.00 a tonne rise in the 1996/97 pool price for all wheat grades, which took Australian Standard White to A$195.00. It also downgraded the forecast 1997/98 wheat crop to 14-15 million tonnes.
Brendan Hillary of ANZ Futures Ltd said SFE contracts were at least A$17.00 a tonne overvalued against the pool price because of drought concern, which was possibly over-blown.
If good recent rain in Western Australia reached the east coast, even half an inch could turn the crop around, he said.
Hillary also said SFE wheat was at least A$30.00 above normal basis trading compared with Chicago, but downside may not materialise while drought persisted, he said.
Australia would produce enough wheat in 1997/98 to meet local demand, but the AWB would also be competing for wheat to export. This could create an artificial shortage, he said.
